per_question.wiki_answer: The minimum BLE connection interval introduced in Bluetooth Core Specification 6.2 is 375 µs. This is achieved by reducing the connection interval unit from 1.25 ms to 125 µs, with the minimum being N × 125 µs where N ≥ 3. Prior to 6.2, the minimum was 7.5 ms (N × 1.25 ms, N ≥ 6). The new interval is configured via the HCI_LE_Connection_Rate_Request command (opcode 0x20A1), which accepts Connection_Interval_Min/Max in units of 125 µs. [Core 6.2, Vol 6, Part B, §4.6.50; Vol 4, Part E, §7.8.154]

per_question.wiki_answer: Bluetooth Core Specification 5.1 first introduced Direction Finding using Angle of Arrival (AoA) and Angle of Departure (AoD). It requires an antenna array: in AoA mode the receiver has the array; in AoD mode the transmitter has the array. The Constant Tone Extension (CTE) is appended after the CRC, enabling IQ sampling by the receiver. [Core 5.1, Vol 1, Part A, §8.1–8.2; Vol 6, Part B, §2.5.1–2.5.4]

per_question.wiki_answer: Connection Subrating (BLE 5.3): Effective_Interval = Connection_Interval × Subrate_Factor × (1 + Continuation_Number). Example: CI=100 ms, SF=10, CN=1 → 100 × 10 × (1+1) = 2000 ms effective wakeup. Supervision_Timeout must be > 2 × CI × SF × (Max_Latency + 1). Recommended: ≥ 6 × Effective_Interval. No renegotiation needed; enables burst-then-sleep pattern. [Core 5.3/5.4, Vol 6, Part B, §4.6.35]

per_question.wiki_answer: Effective_Interval = 100 ms × 10 × (1+1) = 2000 ms. Strict minimum (Max_Latency=0): > 2 × CI × SF × 1 = 2 × 2000 = 4,000 ms. Wiki recommended: ≥ 6 × Effective_Interval = 12,000 ms. Note: Continuation_Number (0–15) extends active window; Max_Latency (0–499) is peripheral latency in subrated events and applies separately to the strict formula. [Core 6.2, Vol 4, Part E, §7.8.123; ble-parameters.md]
